article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Gorilla Butter F2 phenotype
Breeder: Fresh Coast Seed Co.
THC Content: 24–30%
CBD Content: very low
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , limonene , humulene
Primary Flavors: Earth, nuts, pepper, diesel, skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 63–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Moderate to challenging

Some cannabis cultivars become famous because a breeder deliberately launches them under a carefully developed name. White Truffle followed a less conventional path. Its reputation grew around an exceptional selection found within Fresh Coast Seed Co.’s Gorilla Butter genetics, where unusually dark foliage, a near-white blanket of resin and a savory terpene profile separated the plant from more conventional dessert weed.

The result looks almost theatrical when cultivated well: charcoal-purple leaves frame thickly frosted flowers while the aroma moves away from straightforward fruit or candy and into earth, nuts, fuel, spice and funk. Behind that striking appearance is a potent indica-leaning experience that develops in stages, beginning noticeably in the head before gradually spreading into a heavier physical calm.
Genetics and Lineage

Understanding White Truffle requires separating the original genetics from the famous phenotype. Fresh Coast Seed Co. created Gorilla Butter from GG4 and Peanut Butter Breath , two parents with very different but complementary qualities. GG4 contributes the glue-like resin production, fuel-heavy aroma and potency associated with its enormous popularity, while Peanut Butter Breath introduces savory, nutty and earthy characteristics. Fresh Coast later worked the Gorilla Butter line through additional generations, and the selection that became known as White Truffle emerged from Gorilla Butter F2 material. Fresh Coast itself now references both Gorilla Butter and the White Truffle cut as important parts of its breeding history.

That distinction matters because strain databases occasionally give conflicting breeder information or describe White Truffle as though GG4 and Peanut Butter Breath were crossed specifically under that name. A more precise description is that it represents a prized expression of the Gorilla Butter family. Genetic databases likewise identify Gorilla Butter F2 as closely associated with the White Truffle name, while preservation growers describe the clone as GG4 × Peanut Butter Breath. This background also explains why plants sold as White Truffle seeds by unrelated companies may not perfectly reproduce the original clone-only selection.
Effects and Experience

The experience tends to arrive faster than its heavy indica reputation might suggest. Early effects are often concentrated around the head, bringing a buzzing change in perception, an easier mood and a temporary reduction in mental clutter. Conversation may feel more fluid, music more absorbing and routine evening activities more engaging. This strain produces a quick head high that eventually expands into full-body relaxation, which fits the commonly described progression better than simply labeling it sedating from the first inhale.

Physical relaxation becomes increasingly important as the session develops. Tension may soften through the shoulders and limbs while motivation for strenuous activity declines, particularly after larger amounts. That transition makes the strain more naturally suited to late-day marijuana use than productivity-heavy mornings. Potency also deserves respect: tested commercial examples have appeared around 24% THC and into the upper 20% range, while other producers have reported 27–30%, illustrating how significantly cannabis chemistry can differ between harvests. Because THC can impair coordination, judgment and reaction time, consumption should never be paired with driving or other safety-sensitive tasks.
Medical Benefits

The relaxing character of White Truffle has made it attractive to some medical marijuana consumers dealing with discomfort, stress, appetite problems or difficulty settling down at night. Its combination of strong THC and gradually deepening physical effects may be particularly appealing to patients who already tolerate potent cannabis. Broader clinical research has found that some cannabis and cannabinoid preparations can provide modest improvements in chronic pain for certain patients, although evidence concerns cannabis products generally rather than White Truffle specifically. No clinical trial has established this individual cultivar as a treatment for pain, insomnia, anxiety or another medical condition.

High THC can also work against the desired result. While one person may experience mental quiet and relaxation, another may encounter racing thoughts, anxiety, dizziness or excessive sedation. Reviews of THC and anxiety research indicate that THC can produce anxiety-related effects, particularly as dose increases, and NIDA notes that high amounts of marijuana can cause fear, anxiety or panic in susceptible individuals. Patients should therefore judge the actual cannabinoid label rather than assuming that every product carrying the White Truffle name will behave identically, and medical use should be discussed with a qualified healthcare professional when medications or significant health conditions are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

White Truffle occupies the savory side of contemporary cannabis. Breaking apart a cured flower can release damp earth, roasted nuts, pepper and skunk before sharper fuel and garlic-like tones emerge. A faint sweetness may sit underneath, but it rarely dominates the way it does in fruit-forward strains. The unusual mixture helps explain the “truffle” comparison: the bouquet has a dark, earthy character rather than tasting literally like culinary truffles. GG4 ancestry supplies much of the acrid diesel and glue-like background, while the Peanut Butter Breath side complements it with nutty, herbal and soil-like qualities. Fresh Coast describes Gorilla Butter itself as having creamy, earthy-diesel terpene expression.

Terpene testing also varies considerably among producers. Caryophyllene, limonene and humulene frequently appear in published White Truffle profiles, while preserved examples additionally show alpha- and beta-pinene. Caryophyllene reinforces pepper and dry spice, limonene can brighten an otherwise heavy aroma, humulene contributes woody-herbal depth, and pinene can add fresh resinous edges. Because terpene ratios respond to genetics, cultivation, harvest timing and storage, laboratory results from the flower being purchased remain more informative than a universal strain profile.
Growing Information

A mature White Truffle plant is remembered as much for appearance as aroma. Dense flowers develop underneath an exceptional coating of glandular trichomes, creating the pale, frosted appearance behind the name. Dark purple or nearly black foliage may develop around the flowers, with brown-to-orange pistils cutting through the resin-covered surface. This plant features dense, spade-shaped buds, deep purple foliage and heavy white trichome coverage. The original genetic line can be cultivated indoors, outdoors or in greenhouse environments, while records for the White Truffle/Gorilla Butter selection place indoor maturity at roughly 63–70 days and outdoor harvest near the middle of October.

Yield is better described as moderate than enormous, and no dependable original-breeder grams-per-square-meter figure exists for the celebrated cut. Growers should prioritize flower quality, airflow and canopy management rather than treating it as a maximum-output commercial cultivar. Dense resinous buds can trap moisture late in bloom, so maintaining circulation and avoiding excessive humidity becomes increasingly important as flowers swell. The plant’s heavy trichome production also makes careful handling worthwhile during harvest. Environmental control, appropriate feeding and sufficient light can reward the cultivator with exceptionally attractive weed, but preserving the original cut’s color, resin and terpene intensity requires more attention than many beginner-oriented varieties.
FAQ
Is White Truffle indica or sativa?

White Truffle is generally classified as an indica-dominant hybrid. Genetic-preservation records identify the GG4 × Peanut Butter Breath selection as indica dominant, while consumer databases likewise place it on the relaxing side of the hybrid spectrum.
What strain is White Truffle crossed with?

The original lineage traces to Gorilla Butter, bred by Fresh Coast Seed Co. from GG4 × Peanut Butter Breath. White Truffle is most accurately described as a prized Gorilla Butter F2 selection rather than an entirely separate two-parent cross.
How strong is White Truffle weed?

Potency varies considerably by producer. Commercial examples have tested around 24% THC, while other cultivated batches reach approximately 27–30%. Consumers should always use the laboratory result printed on the specific product.
What does White Truffle taste like?

Its profile is predominantly earthy and savory, with nutty, peppery, skunky and diesel notes accompanied by occasional garlic, pine and mild sweetness. Caryophyllene, limonene, humulene and pinene commonly contribute to the aromatic profile.
How long does White Truffle take to flower?

The original-style cut generally finishes indoors in approximately 63–70 days. Outdoor cultivation commonly reaches maturity around mid-October under an appropriate Northern Hemisphere growing season.
Final Thoughts on White Truffle

White Truffle stands out because its reputation was built around a particular expression of cannabis genetics rather than simply an appealing name. Fresh Coast Seed Co.’s GG4 × Peanut Butter Breath foundation produced Gorilla Butter, and the exceptional F2 selection associated with White Truffle amplified the family’s strongest visual and aromatic traits: heavy resin, dark coloration, savory earth, nuts, pepper and fuel. Its effects follow an equally distinctive curve, moving from an immediate cerebral buzz into a slower, more substantial physical calm.

For experienced consumers, that combination of potency, unusual flavor and evening-friendly relaxation explains much of the cultivar’s lasting appeal. Growers encounter a plant valued more for resin quality and striking flower than sheer production, while connoisseurs receive a profile dramatically different from the candy and tropical fruit genetics that dominate many modern menus. Most importantly, understanding White Truffle as the celebrated Gorilla Butter selection helps preserve the genetic history behind one of the more recognizable boutique marijuana cultivars of its generation.
